body:
maria: Heads-up — Jordan asked about carrying over PTO after parental leave that overlaps the company shutdown blackout. Can we consider a soft-cap exception?
jordan: Hey @maria — I'm due in Dec and will be on parental leave through year-end. My team hits the Q4 shutdown (mandatory time-off). I won't be able to take my remaining ~10 PTO days earlier. Is there a path to carry them beyond the normal cap?
sam: Quick note: payroll auto-pays carryover above the cap (last I checked). That usually applies on Jan payroll.
ben: Confirming — standard carryover cap is 5 days. Anything above 5 is auto-paid out on the first payroll of the new year. Exceptions are allowed but require People Ops + manager approval; >5 days also needs executive signoff for accounting.
maria: Copying the relevant policy excerpt below for context:
```
Carryover Policy (excerpt):
- Employees may roll over up to 5 days of unused PTO to the next calendar year.
- Unused PTO beyond 5 days will be paid out on the first payroll in January.
- Exceptions: documented LOA (medical/parental) which prevents taking PTO during the year may be eligible for temporary carryover at People Ops discretion with manager and exec approval.
```
maria: Jordan — please submit an exception request using the HR Exception form (https://intranet.redwood/hr/forms/pto-exception). Include LOA dates, expected return-to-work, and a short manager note. I'll route to Ben for payroll annotation and to Execs for signoff. Filing deadline for this year's window is Dec 15.
jordan: Thanks. Two quick Qs: 1) If approved, will the days sit as PTO in the next year's balance or as a special tracked bucket? 2) Any effect on benefits accruals or probationary period?
maria: If approved we mark them as "temporary carryover" on your balance for Q1; payroll will flag them so they don't auto-pay. Benefits and standard accruals remain unchanged. No impact to probation.
ben: Also note: if the year-end shutdown is designated as mandatory company time-off, policy prefers folks use PTO where possible. Exceptions are considered for extended LOA that overlaps the entire window. We need documentation to process >5 days.
jordan: Filing the form now and attaching the LOA confirmation from my manager.
hr-bot: Reminder: attach LOA documentation when submitting the exception form. Missing docs delay review.
sam: fyi if exec signoff needed it can take up to a week depending on calendar.
maria: I'll acknowledge when I receive the form and provide an expected ETA. Will loop in Legal/Benefits if anything looks edge-case.
jordan: Appreciate it — thanks everyone.
maria: will update thread once decision made. :thumbsup:
